summary: Dmitry Kudryavsky (1867–1920) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at St. Petersburg University under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev (Ivan Minayev) from circa 1886 to 1890. He held a post at the University of Tartu from circa 1898 to 1918.
Do Trul Tubten Changchub Gyaltsen is a scholar who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.

Dodrupchen Rinpoche (1927–2022) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Kunzang Pelden, and Jigdrel Changchub Dorje, and taught Ronald M. Davidson, Tulku Thondup, and several others.

Dominic Goodall is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed his D.Phil. at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, taught at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (2005), and held posts at Wolfson College and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (2000).

Dominic Sur is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard and the University of Virginia, completing his doctorate under David Germano, Karen Christina Lang, Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and Khenpo Lama Chönam. He joined Utah State University (attested 2017).

Dominik Haas specializes in Indology and religious studies, completing doctoral work under Marion Rastelli. He has held positions as a DOC Fellow at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia and at the University of Vienna (attested 2022).

Dominik Wujastyk is an Indologist educated at the University of London and University of Oxford. His career includes posts at the Wellcome Institute (~1984–2014), University College London (2002–2009), the University of Vienna (2009–2015), and the University of Alberta (2015).

Dominique Sportiche (born 1952) is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from circa 1978 to 1984. He held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles, beginning around 1987.

Dominique-Sila Khan (1949–2016) was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied at Paris-Sorbonne University and served as a Research Fellow at the Institute of Rajasthan Studies (attested 2000).
Don A. Pittman specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He pursued doctoral studies at the University of Chicago and served on the faculty at Texas Christian University.

Don Handelman (born 1939) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at McGill University, the University of Pittsburgh, and the University of Manchester before becoming Professor of Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem around 1972.

Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe (1865–1937) was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He studied at Richmond College and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, served as epigraphist for the Government of Ceylon (~1899–1928), and held a post at the University of London (~1917–1930).

Donald A. Ringe (born 1954) is a linguist who earned his PhD at Yale under Warren Crawford Cowgill. After teaching Classics at Bard College (1983–1985), he joined the linguistics faculty at the University of Pennsylvania in 1985.

Donald E. Gjertson (born 1944) is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford University under John Ching-yu Wang and Akira Takeda, later serving on the faculty at the University of Massachusetts Amherst (~1976–2012).

Donald Eric Capps (1939–2015) was a religious studies scholar educated at Lewis & Clark, Yale, and the University of Chicago. He taught at Chicago, UNC Charlotte, Phillips University, and was Professor of Pastoral Theology at Princeton Theological Seminary (1981–2009).
Donald Harper is a sinologist who held posts at the University of Arizona (attested 1999) and the University of Chicago, where he served as Centennial Professor of Chinese Studies (attested 2026).

Donald K. Swearer (born 1934) is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar mentored by Kenneth K. S. Ch'en and Singkha Wannasai. He held posts at Swarthmore College (~1970–2004), Chiang Mai University, and Harvard University (2004–2010).

Donald Keene (1922–2019) was a Japanologist who studied at Columbia University under Wm. Theodore de Bary and at Harvard. He held academic posts at the University of Cambridge (1949–1954) and Columbia University from 1955.

Donald Phillip Verene (born 1937) is a philosopher educated at Knox College and Washington University in St. Louis. He served as Chair at Emory University (1982–1988) and held visiting appointments at Pembroke College, Oxford, and Sapienza University of Rome.

Donald R. Davis Jr. is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Patrick Olivelle, Ludo Rocher, and Richard W. Lariviere. He held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2006–2012) and the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).
